survivors.claim: The extraction grammar only recognises `git` preceded by line start, `;&|(` backtick, or whitespace, so a path-prefixed or backslash-escaped invocation (`/usr/bin/git commit`, `\git commit`) is never extracted and passes under an open wave. This is the grammar the spec's Contracts block locks (A4 lists 16 observed samples, none path-prefixed), so it is a sanctioned gap, not a violation — recorded so the known-gap paragraph in Rationale can name it beside the cd-into-another-tree gap.
survivors.impact: A worker that spells out the full path to the version-control binary is not stopped by the new guard.
survivors.evidence: RE at line 35: `(^|[;&|(\`]|[[:space:]])git(...)` — `/` is in none of the admitted predecessor classes; spec Contracts lines 93-102 lock this exact regex and list only `gitk`/`digit add`/quoted forms as the observed non-matches. Not executed (sandbox refused the probe); reported soft.

survivors.claim: A `-c key="value with space"` global option breaks the option-skipping alternation at the space, so the next word of the quoted value is extracted as the verb and the BLOCKED line names it (e.g. `git -c user.name="a b" commit` → `BLOCKED: git b …`). Direction is safe (it still blocks) but the remedy line misnames the verb.
survivors.impact: In one unusual spelling the refusal message names the wrong word as the offending verb, which makes the diagnostic misleading though the block itself is correct.
survivors.evidence: Line 35: `-c[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+` stops at the first space inside the quoted value; the trailing `[[:space:]]+[a-z][a-z-]*` then captures `b`; line 41 takes it as the verb; `b` is outside ALLOW (line 34) → block naming `b`. Grammar reading, not executed.

survivors.claim: The marker-path derivation (`git -C <root> rev-parse --git-dir`, absolutize against root when relative, join `spec-wave-open`) is written out four times in this diff — driver `syncWaveMarker`, `tests/worker-git-hook.test.js::fixture`, `tests/consistency/red-fixture-coverage.test.js::hookWorkerGit`, `tests/build/build-driver-wave-marker.test.js::markerOf` — which meets the pipeline rules' three-or-more duplication calibration; a `waveMarkerPath(root)` helper in `tests/helpers.js` is the extraction for the three test copies.
survivors.impact: Three test files each re-derive the same marker location by hand, so a future change to where the marker lives must be made in four places and a miss in one goes unnoticed.
